newsitem.title: USA: Founder's group asks Figgie reconsider plan.
newsitem.headline: Founder's group asks Figgie reconsider plan.

text.p: A shareholder group led by Harry Figgie Jr., founder of Figgie International Inc, on Monday urged the company to reconsider its "deconglomeration" strategy.
The group, which controls a stake of about 20 percent in the Willoughby, Oh.,-based company, made its stand known in a letter to the Figgie board by its financial advisor, Batchelder & Partners Inc.

"We are concerned that the board's oversight of the company's (Figgie's) efforts to enhance shareholder value through a restructuring has led to a seriously suboptimal share price while exposing the strongest divisions of the company to continued market risk," Batchelder said.

The group's concerns come after an announcement by Figgie on October 16 that it would divest its Taylor Environmental unit and focus on its three core businesses, Snorkel, Scott Aviation and Interstate Electronics.
As previously reported, Harry Figgie is no longer with the company and is seeking to maximize shareholder value, including the possible merger or sale of Figgie's assets.
In its letter, Batchelder noted that Figgie's class B share price has declined by about 40 percent since hitting a high of $15.50 in June.

While noting that the "significant conglomerate discount" was not uncommon when disparate busineses are combined in one entity, Batchelder said it is convinced that "several straight forward, common sense solutions to this problem exist and are readily available to the (Figgie) board."

"We are confident that serious reconsideration ot a deconglomeration strategy, with the benefit of information you possess, could result in a tailered plan yielding several dollars per share increase in the company's common stock price," Batchelder added.
Batchelder said it requested a meeting with the Figgie board before the company's annual meeting scheduled for November 26.
